plain.headline: Love God, Love Neighbor
plain.intro: Today a lawyer asks Jesus which commandment matters most, and Jesus gives two: love God with everything, and love your neighbor as yourself. The first reading shows what that love looks like in practice, in God's care for strangers, widows, orphans and the poor. Paul's letter shows a young church that turned to God and became an example to everyone around it.
plain.listen: the two commandments that hold up all the others

Reading 1.box: God gives Israel laws that protect the people with the least power: foreigners, widows, orphans and the poor. God says he hears their cry and takes their side. These laws come from the covenant God made with Israel at Mount Sinai, after freeing them from slavery in Egypt.

chunks.text: Anyone who offers sacrifice to any god other than the Lord will be destroyed.
Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner. You were foreigners yourselves in Egypt. Do not take advantage of a widow or an orphan.
If you do, and they cry out to me, I will hear them. My anger will burn, and you will die by the sword. Then your own wives will be widows and your own children orphans.
If you lend money to one of my people who is poor, do not act like a moneylender. Do not charge interest. If you take your neighbor's coat as a pledge, give it back before sunset.

Responsorial Psalm.box: The psalmist tells God, "I love you," and calls him a rock, a fortress and a rescuer. He praises the living God who saved him from his enemies and keeps faith with the king he chose.

Reading 2.box: Paul thanks God for the Christians in Thessalonica, who welcomed the Gospel with joy even while they suffered for it. Word of their faith spread across Greece. This letter, written around the year 50, is probably the oldest writing in the New Testament.

chunks.text: The Good News reached you not just as words but with power, with the Holy Spirit and with deep conviction. You saw how we lived among you for your good. You followed our example and the Lord's. You accepted the word in the middle of great trouble, with the joy the Holy Spirit gives.

So you became a model for all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia. The Lord's word has rung out from you, not only there but everywhere. People everywhere know about your faith in God, so we have nothing to add.

They tell others how you welcomed us, and how you turned away from idols to serve the living and true God. Now you wait for his Son to come from heaven. God raised him from the dead. He is Jesus, who rescues us from the judgment to come.

Gospel.box: In Jerusalem, a few days before his death, Jesus is tested by religious leaders. Asked for the greatest commandment, he joins two from the Jewish Law: love of God from Deuteronomy and love of neighbor from Leviticus. He says everything else in Scripture rests on them.

chunks.text: The Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, so they met together. One of them, an expert in the Law, tried to test him. "Teacher," he asked, "which commandment in the Law is the greatest?"
Jesus answered, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the greatest and first commandment.
The second is like it: Love your neighbor as yourself. All of the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments."

plain.carry: Love for God shows up in how we treat the person who has the least.

kids.headline: The Two Biggest Rules
kids.intro: Today someone asks Jesus which of God's rules is the most important. Jesus says the biggest rules are to love God with all your heart and to love other people as much as you love yourself.
kids.listen: Listen for the word "love" in the Gospel and count how many times you hear it.

Reading 1.box: God gives his people rules to protect people who could easily be hurt, like newcomers from other lands, children without parents, and poor families. God says he always hears them when they cry for help.

chunks.text: God says: Worship only me, not other gods. People who turn to false gods will be punished. Be kind to people who come from other lands, because you once lived in a land that was not yours. Never take advantage of a woman whose husband has died or a child who has no parents.
If you hurt them and they cry to me, I will hear them. I will be very angry, and the person who hurt them will be punished with death, so that their own family will know what it is to lose someone.
If you lend money to someone poor, do not make them pay back extra. If you keep someone's coat until they pay you back, return it before night so they are not cold.

Responsorial Psalm.box: The person singing this song tells God, "I love you." God is like a strong rock and a safe castle who keeps him safe.

Reading 2.box: Paul writes a letter to a church in a city called Thessalonica. He is happy because the people there believed in Jesus with joy, even when it was hard, and now people everywhere are talking about their faith.

chunks.text: When we told you about Jesus, the Holy Spirit worked in a powerful way. You saw how we lived, and you copied us and the Lord. Things were hard for you, but the Holy Spirit gave you joy. Now you are an example for everyone who believes in your whole region.

People everywhere have heard about your faith in God. They tell how you stopped praying to statues and started serving the real, living God. Now you wait for Jesus to come back from heaven. God raised him from the dead, and he saves us.

Gospel.box: Some leaders want to trick Jesus with a hard question. Jesus gives an answer so good that it sums up everything God has ever asked of us.

chunks.text: Some leaders called Pharisees came together. One of them, who knew God's law very well, wanted to test Jesus. He asked, "Teacher, which of God's rules is the most important?"

Jesus said, "Love God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your mind. That is the first and most important rule. The second one is like it: Love other people as much as you love yourself. All of God's other rules grow out of these two."

word.meaning: A commandment is a rule God gives us to help us love him and each other.

kids.draw: Draw a big heart with God at the top and the people you love inside it.
kids.ask: Who is someone you could show God's love to this week?

family.opener: Today Jesus tells us that the two most important things God asks are to love him and to love other people.
questions: What does it look like to love God with all your heart?
Who are the people near us who might feel left out or alone?
Why do you think Jesus put loving God and loving others side by side?
family.try: Together, choose one person who could use some kindness this week, and do something for them as a family.
family.pray: Lord, help our family love you with all our hearts and love each person you put in our path.
